gmat.epoch: A time of the flight is not in the range of GMAT (1957-10-04 to 2100-02-28).
gmat.option: An option of the script is incorrect. The name of the spacecraft must start with a letter and have only letters, digits and the character "_".
gmat.model: The force model has no Sun. The script integrates relative to the Sun.
gmat.maneuver: The application cannot find the velocity change of a maneuver in a local frame. Calculate the flight again.
gmat.srpRange: GMAT does not accept this reflectivity coefficient or this area. The coefficient must be from 0 to 2, and the area must be more than zero.

gmatDiff.ephemeris: The body positions come from the ephemeris of GMAT (default: DE405), not from the data of this application (DE440).
gmatDiff.j2: The script does not have the oblateness (J2) of the planets.
gmatDiff.moons: The script does not have the large moons as separate masses.
gmatDiff.smallBodies: GMAT does not have Ceres, Vesta and Psyche. The script does not have their gravity.
gmatDiff.reducedModel: The force model does not have all the planets. This application integrates relative to the solar system barycenter. GMAT integrates relative to the Sun.
gmatDiff.srp: The solar radiation pressure of GMAT is different code with a shadow model.
gmatDiff.relativity: The relativistic correction of GMAT is different code.
gmatDiff.anchors: A maneuver has a stored state of the flight solver. GMAT continues from the state that it calculated. After some flybys, its path can be far from the path of this application.

file.read.title: Value from a file
file.read.method: The application read this value from the text that you gave. It converts times to TDB and states to km and km/s. It makes no other change to the values.
file.read.limit: The value has the accuracy of the file. In the tests, the readers give the numbers of JPL Horizons tables and of CCSDS, STK and CSV files. No error is larger than the last digit of the file.

file.approach.title: Closest approach from a table
file.approach.method: The application finds the sample of the table that is nearest to the body. It propagates the state of the sample before it to the sample after it in the default force model. The closest approach of that propagation is the result. The column "Distance from the next sample" shows the difference between the propagation and the file.
file.approach.limit: The test is the flyby of Venus by Cassini. The result from a JPL Horizons table with 1-day samples is 0.0076 km from the closest approach in the 1-minute table. A maneuver between the two samples is not in the result: then the distance from the next sample is large.

file.check.title: Interpolation error of the table
file.check.method: At the center of the interval between two samples, the application calculates the position from an interpolation in the table (Hermite, degree 7, 4 samples). It compares this position with the flight. The flight position comes from a new integration from the nearest step of the integrator, not from an interpolation.
file.check.limit: The check examines not more than 400 intervals: the intervals where the path bends most, and intervals at equal distances. A program that uses a different interpolation method gets a different error.

file.difference.title: Distance between the flight and the file
file.difference.method: At the time of each sample of the file, the application calculates the position of the flight and its distance from the sample. It uses no interpolation in the file.
file.difference.limit: The flight position has the accuracy of the propagation: refer to the Propagation screen. The sample has the accuracy of the file.

horizonsCenter.title: JPL Horizons tables of a spacecraft relative to the barycenter
horizonsCenter.text: For Cassini in 1999 and for Juno in 2013, the JPL Horizons tables relative to the Sun and to the Earth agree. The table relative to the solar system barycenter is 118 km (Cassini) and 117 km (Juno) from them. For the flyby of the Earth by Cassini, the table relative to the barycenter gives an altitude that is 86 km too small. A possible cause is that Horizons uses a different planet file for the barycenter. There is no check of this cause. Use a table relative to the Sun or to the planet of the flyby.

tables.title: Trajectory tables with a fixed step
tables.text: A table with a fixed step has large interpolation errors at a flyby. For the flight of Voyager 2, a table with 1-day samples has an error of 149 000 km at Neptune. The table with the steps of the integrator has an error of 0.06 km with a third of the samples. The Files screen shows this error before it writes a file.

files.title: Files
files.intro: This screen reads trajectory files of other programs and writes the flight for other programs. The application does all the work on this computer: it does not send a file to a server.
files.readNote: Formats: CCSDS OEM and OPM, STK ephemeris, JPL Horizons vector table, CSV table, and the mission file of this application.
files.moveNote: You can also move a file onto this panel, or put the text of a file in the field below.
files.tooLarge: The file is larger than {n} MB. The application does not read it.
files.found: The application found the format from the text.
files.notFound: The application cannot find the format of this text. Select the format.
files.csvOptions: Data that a CSV table does not contain
files.horizonsOptions: Data for a Horizons text with no header
files.optScaleHint: The application uses this value only if the name of the time column does not give the time scale.
files.optUnitHint: The application uses this value only if the column names do not give the unit.
files.errorTitle: The application cannot read this file.
files.ssbNote: This Horizons table of a spacecraft is relative to the solar system barycenter. For Cassini and Juno, tables of this type are 118 km and 117 km from the tables relative to the Sun and to a planet. For the flyby of the Earth by Cassini, this difference makes the altitude 86 km too small. Get a table relative to the Sun or to the planet of the flyby: refer to the Accuracy screen.
files.approachesIntro: The samples of a file are frequently far from each other at a flyby. For each closest approach, the application propagates the state of the sample before it to the sample after it. The values come from that propagation, not from an interpolation.
files.missWarn: At {body} ({time} {scale}), the propagation does not agree with the next sample of the file. Possible causes are a maneuver between the two samples or a force that the force model does not have. A different cause is too much time between the samples for a low flyby. The values of this closest approach are approximate.
files.noApproach: The table has no closest approach to a body of the force model.
files.moreApproaches: The table shows the first {n} closest approaches.
files.boundaries: The file shows these maneuvers: two samples with the same time and different velocities.
files.noBoundaries: The file shows no maneuver as two samples with the same time.
files.search: Search for maneuvers between the samples
files.searchIntro: The application propagates each sample to the next sample. A velocity at the end that does not agree with the file shows a maneuver or a force that is not in the model.
files.noise: Median velocity difference of all intervals
files.noiseHint: The median is the noise of this table in the force model of the application.
files.skippedHint: An interval has no result if its propagation goes into a body or is not in the date range of the data.
files.flybyNote: An interval with a flyby makes a small error much larger. A result for an interval of this type is frequently not a maneuver.
files.searchNone: The search found no interval above the limit.
files.makeMission: Make a mission from this trajectory
files.spanNote: The start and the end are samples of the file: the application uses the sample that is nearest to your time.
files.makeNote: The new flight starts at the state of the start sample and has the maneuvers that you select. It is a propagation in the force model of the application: it is not a copy of the samples of the file. The graph on this screen then shows the distance between the flight and the file. A flyby makes a small difference much larger: use the targeter on the Maneuvers screen to aim the flight at the closest approaches of the file.
files.compare: Compare with the flight of the mission
files.compareNote: The Mission and Propagation screens then show the trajectory of the file as a dashed line.
files.noCoverage: The first sample is not in the date range of the ephemeris data. The application cannot propagate from it.
files.difference: Flight of the mission and trajectory of the file
files.differenceIntro: Each value is the distance between the flight and a sample of the file at the time of the sample. The comparison uses no interpolation in the file.
files.diffLabel: Distance between the flight and the samples of the file
files.diffNone: No sample of the file is in the time of the flight.
files.removeReference: Remove the trajectory of the file
files.opm: State and maneuvers of the file
files.opmSrp: Area and coefficient for solar radiation pressure
files.opmMake: Make a mission from this state
files.opmMakeNote: An OPM has no force model: the flight uses the default force model of the application. The spacecraft of the mission has the default values. Change them on the Mission screen.
files.write: Write the flight to a file
files.noMission: No mission is open. Open or make a mission first.
files.noFlight: This mission has no flight. Calculate the flight on the Mission screen. You can write the mission file with no flight.
files.flightOld: The plan changed after the last flight calculation. The file has the flight, not the plan.
files.objectIdHint: CCSDS recommends the international designator: launch year, launch number and part letter (YYYY-NNNP).
files.frameFixed: This format has the states in the ICRF.
files.scaleFixed: This format has its times in seconds after an epoch in UTC.
files.samplingNote: The integrator makes short steps near a body and long steps in cruise. A table with these steps is small and has samples where the path bends. A table with a fixed step can have large interpolation errors at a flyby.
files.gmatAxes: GMAT axes for the ICRF numbers
files.gmatAxesNote: The GMAT user guide does not give the axes in which GMAT uses its planet data. The default (MJ2000Eq) is correct if GMAT uses this data as MJ2000Eq vectors with no rotation. If the selection is incorrect, the error is less than 24 km at 1 au. This limit comes from a value in the user guide.
files.gmatSetGm: Set the GM of each body to the value of this application
files.gmatSourceHint: For example DE421. Empty: the default of GMAT.
files.gmatDifferences: Differences between this flight and the flight of the script in GMAT
files.opmNote: An OPM has the start state and the impulsive maneuvers of the flight. It has no force model: the program that reads it uses the force model of that program.
files.opmMassNote: The file has the mass at the start of the flight ({mass}). The specific impulse ({isp}) gives the change of mass of each maneuver.
files.missionNote: The mission file keeps the plan, the flight, the spacecraft and your bodies. Only this application reads it.
files.checkText: Largest distance between the flight and an interpolation in this table
files.checkBad: A program that reads this table cannot get the flight from it with an error of less than 1 km. Use the steps of the integrator, more samples between the steps, or a smaller step.
files.checkGood: A program that reads this table with this interpolation gets the flight with an error of less than 1 km.
files.notVerified: No test opened these files in STK or in GMAT, because these programs were not available. The tests read each file again with the readers of this application: refer to the Accuracy screen.
files.commentModel: Trajectory from a numerical integration. Ephemeris: DE440 (fit of {app}).
